To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean cluster virial-mass--richness relation is consistent with LCDM models and that the halo concentration and halo bias are consistent with LCDM predictions.

(1) the mass of a cluster of galaxies can be inferred from its optical richness or luminosity, with a precision of 13% including all sources of error; (2) the mean density profile of a cluster of given richness or luminosity has a universal shape, which is well described by a single parameter (the concentration) that depends on mass; and (3) the mass of clusters of a given richness or luminosis is well described by an N-body simulation of LCDM,
the cluster-mass function is well described by the halo mass function, and the mean cluster density/mass profile is well described by a NFW profile.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the statistical weak lens shear signal around clusters of galaxies, with the ultimate aim of using the cluster mass--richness relation to constrain the dark energy equation of state.
the use of weak lensing measurements of galaxy cluster mass profiles and mass--richness relation to constrain the cosmological parameters of the universe and the nature of dark energy.

the statistical properties of the dark matter distribution in clusters of galaxies, and with the relation between cluster mass and optical properties that can be measured with current and future surveys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the weak lensing results are consistent with LCDM cosmology, and are consistent with the cluster mass function, but are not yet sufficiently constraining to rule out other cosmologies.
the cluster mass--richness relation is well determined and in agreement with LCDM predictions.
the weak lensing results presented in this paper are in good agreement (to within 20%) with the results of numerical N-body simulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cluster mass--richness and luminosity relations are robustly measured and can be used as a powerful cosmological probe.

the cluster mass-richness relation is well established, and that the cluster mass-luminosity relation is also well determined for luminous clusters, although there is some uncertainty at the low mass end.

, with the help of N-body simulations and the assumption that the universe is homogeneous and isotropic, the weak lensing measurement of the cluster shear profiles is an effective way to constrain the cluster density profiles, and the cluster density profile is an effective way for us to constrain the cluster-mass profiles, and then we could infer the relation between cluster mass and cluster optical richness.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cluster-mass function can be calibrated using optical richness or luminosity, with the same systematic errors, and that the cluster mass can be inferred from the richness or luminosity with the same systematic uncertainties.
the mean mass profile of a cluster can be inferred from the shear signal around the central galaxy, even if the cluster halo is not precisely centered on the central galaxy.
we can use the cross-correlation between the weak lensing signal from galaxy clusters and the galaxy density field to constrain the mass-richness relation and halo concentration.
